title.narrative: UNDP, 2018-2022, GDPP Governance Program i Ethiopien

description.narrative: Stöd till demokratiska institutioner som lyder under parlamentet i syfte att stärka dess möjligheter att genomföra sitt mandat på ett mer oberoende sätt.
Support to the main accountability mechanism in Ethiopia in order to contribute to that they can implement their core mandate in a more independent and professional manner.

The objectives of the programme, that is managed by the UNDP and implemented by Ethiopian state institutions, including the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission, NEBE, the Ombudsman, The Federal Court, the Anti-Corruption Commission, Ministry of Peace, and the Parliament, to strengthen key democratic functions, are as follows:
1. Political processes of federal and regional state legislative bodies are more inclusive and effectively delivering on their constitutional mandates. 2. Federal and regional state systems of governance are more accountable, transparent and are delivering public services in a more inclusive and responsive ways. 3. Citizens are more empowered to voice their concern and actively participate in decision making processes at all levels of the governance and political systems. 4. Systems and mechanisms for promoting social cohesion, managing diversity, preventing and managing conflicts, fostering dialogues and building peace are further strengthened at national, regional and local levels. 5. Access to justice enhanced and human rights promoted and protected across Ethiopia.

Over the project period, the following eleven Ethiopian democratic institutions/Implementing Partners (IPs) benefited from the GDPP support:
1. House of Peoples Representatives (HoPR)
2. House of Federation (HoF)
3. Federal Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (FEACC)
4. Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC)
5. Ethiopian Institute of Ombudsman (EIO)
6. Office of Attorney General (OAG)
7. Office of Federal Auditor General (OFAG)
8.Ministry of Peace (MoP)
9.Council of Constitutional Inquiry (CCI)
10. National Election Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
11.Ethiopia Media Authority (EMA formerly the Ethiopian Broadcast Authority)
These institutions / partners received the GDPP support in order to increase their efficiency, transparency and inclusivity and thereby improve the quality of the institutions. This implied the aim to strengthen citizens' empowerment and participation, access to justice and protection of human rights.
Examples of results hat the project achieved:
Firstly, in 2020, a new Media Policy for enhanced freedom of expression and strengthened media independence was introduced and adopted by the Council of Ministers. A media monitoring manual and fact-checking guideline was also implemented to strengthen the quality and delivery of its media monitoring and fact checking mandates. This was also combined with UNDP led training for media operators.
Secondly, the Federal Ethics and anti-corruption commission (FEACC) organized forums and trainings for key stakeholders to raise awareness about corruption. The participants of the trainings became equipped with skills & knowledge about corruption, practical approaches and tools on ethical decision-making, organizational integrity, conflict of interest and corruption risk assessment. To ensure sustainability of the program, the training participants gained skills on how to organize and facilitate online training in FEACCs future training programs. The FEACC program also implied a platform between key stakeholders such as municipalities and media institutions to create a conducive environment for a joint action to prevent corruption. This implied raising public awareness to provide reliable information on corruption and for the public to be part of the solution as regards prevention of corruption.
Thirdly, with support of the project, the Ethiopian Institute of Ombudsman (EIO) developed and operationalized a new IT-based case flow management and database systems and familiarized staff with newly developed IT-based systems. These innovations will help to improve the EIO ability to handle individual cases with greater efficiency.
Fourthly, the program also supported the independence, mandate, functioning and activity of the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC) in raising and following up on human rights abuses in Ethiopia. For instance, in November 2023, the EHRC and UN Human Rights Office released a report of the joint investigation of alleged human rights violations related to the Tigray conflict.
